findings.title: Mermaid file open is falsely asserted idempotent
findings.why_it_matters: Clients may automatically retry a tool advertised as idempotent. Each successful open_mermaid_file call imports the Mermaid source into a newly UUID-named BPMN file, so a retry creates another persisted diagram and has an additional environmental effect. The exhaustive tuple test repeats the incorrect expectation without exercising this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Advertise open_mermaid_file with idempotentHint: false (the additive tuple), and add a behavioral probe that opens the same Mermaid fixture twice and asserts two distinct output filenames/files.
evidence: src/server/handlers.ts:298-313 routes every open_mermaid_file call through engine.importXml rather than reopening a stable BPMN target.

src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:931-932 assigns defaultFilename(context) and persists the imported diagram; src/core/SimpleBpmnEngine.ts:1430-1441 includes a fresh IdGenerator.generateUuid() in every default filename.
tests/contracts/tool-annotations.test.ts:52 expects IDEMPOTENT_UPDATE, while the idempotency probe at lines 152-170 exercises only update_element and save.

residual_risks: The tools/list checks for npm start, the optional bundle, and the packed executable were inspected in scripts/package-smoke.mjs but not executed because the review was constrained to be read-only and that script cleans and rebuilds dist.
testing_gaps: Repeat open_mermaid_file with identical arguments and assert that the advertised idempotency value matches the additional UUID-backed persisted file effect.
